**Hands-on Game Director for WHAT THE CAR?

**Do you love working in small, creative teams turning wild ideas into a reality? Do you thrive on community feedback? Could you ensure an already loved comedy game remains goofy in all the right ways? Awesome. We need to talk!

Triband is the award-winning studio behind the WHAT THE? comedy game series, played by millions worldwide. From our home in central Copenhagen, more than 60 wonderful humans are united by a simple mission: to make everyone laugh.

WHAT THE CAR? is our absurdly silly racing adventure game which addresses fundamental questions such as… What if a car had legs? Or a jetpack? Or secretly identified as a sailboat? First launched in 2023 on Apple Arcade and now also on Steam, it has gained a steady following of dedicated fans who have contributed hundreds of thousands of community-built levels.

We’re looking for a Game Director to grab the creative wheel (sorry) on a small but mighty team to help steer CAR into the future. You’ll guide decisions on which jokes are worth pursuing, how we maintain and push quality and which turns to take along the road. You'll work closely with studio creative leadership and external partners to help define the future of CAR and to explore opportunities to reach even bigger audiences.

If you’re already rethinking what a car is, keep reading!

**Here’s What You'll Do Day To Day

**

• Take product responsibility for WHAT THE CAR? and ensure that it remains true to and evolves upon the existing WHAT THE? universe

• Along with studio leadership, define the game’s ongoing vision, strategy and goals

• Effectively communicate the vision within the team to enable team and individual autonomy

• Work closely with the Producer and team to create achievable product roadmaps built upon a humanistic approach to production

• Contribute directly to project development, such as creating prototypes, implementing gameplay or building levels in-engine

• Facilitate team-wide creative processes which ensure all ideas have been heard and the best solutions are agreed and understood

• Ensure we maintain a high quality bar across the game, and help catch what’s not working before it ships

• Be part of nurturing a creative, inclusive, high performing, high trust team culture

• Immerse yourself in user feedback, turning what players tell us into decisions about where the game goes next

**You’re a great match if

**

• You bring 8+ years working in creative product lead roles

• You’ve worked on at least 3 commercial and shipped game projects

• You are extremely familiar with one or more commercial game engines, including Unity

• You're a born communicator and collaborator who enjoys working closely with every member of a team

• You understand and appreciate the WHAT THE? universe and are excited to be an integral part of its future

• You use AI to boost workflows and productivity, giving you more time to focus on the important creative decisions

• You prefer to “show don’t tell” by demonstrating ideas through prototypes over endless design discussions

• You have experience working on family-friendly titles for a casual audience

**Nice to have

**

• Experience coding in C#

• Experience with game design for a live game

• Experience in the mobile premium space

**What Always Matters To Us At Triband

**

• You thrive in taking ownership of your area: you spot problems, seek advice when needed, and implement creative solutions that push projects forward

• You’re motivated by collaboration, mutual respect, inclusiveness and creativity while actively contributing to sustaining that culture

• You believe games are made by teams, not rockstars and that great ideas can come from anyone

• You bring curiosity, generosity, and flexibility, along with strong opinions, especially when they come with reasoning, openness, and a willingness to actually test them

• You love exploration and experimentation but don’t get too precious when the evidence tells you you’re wrong

• You value a positive work environment and contribute to keeping the studio a fun and supportive place to be

**Practicalities

**

• Role based in our cozy office in central Copenhagen

• We want to make sure we find the right person, so we also consider people located outside of Denmark and provide financial (and moral!) relocation support

• This team works with an office-first hybrid model: primarily working together in office with occasional remote working

• We work a 37-hour work week with flexible working hours

• Our working language is English

**We offer

**

• The opportunity to define and shape the future of a beloved game together with a closely knit team where everyone is actively participating in the creative process

• A playful work environment where trying the silly idea is encouraged

• Friendly and kind colleagues who love making each other laugh as much as making games

• A professional development budget to invest in your growth

• Social activities like Friday bars, hobby nights, board game nights, and whatever else Tribanders turn into a tradition

• Daily lunch at a local restaurant, with plant-based options and soft ice on Thursdays

• Private health insurance paid by us

• Child's first sick day on us, no questions asked

• Endless amounts of Club Mate

**WHAT THE TRIBAND?

**Triband is the award-winning studio behind the WHAT THE? comedy game series, played by millions worldwide.

From our home in central Copenhagen, more than 60 wonderful humans are united by our mission to make people laugh. We explore comedy through gameplay, which means we like to break player expectations, create surprising interactions, use great music and slick art, and build quirky worlds full of personality.

We put people first and strive to create a safe and creative working environment. We believe that teams, not individuals, make games. And we believe diversity makes teams better. For these reasons, we look for people who bring new perspectives and who are excited to challenge us and our way of doing things.

For more info about Triband, check out: triband.net/about

At ABB, we help industries run leaner and cleaner—and every person here makes that happen. You’ll be empowered to lead, supported to grow, and proud of the impact we create together. Join us and help run what runs the world.

This position reports to:

Product Marketing Manager

__

What we believe in:

At ABB, we are dedicated to addressing global challenges head-on. Our core values: care, courage, curiosity, and collaboration - combined with a focus on diversity, inclusion, and equal opportunities - are important drivers in our goal to enable everyone to create sustainable solutions. This is our story. Make it your story.

Role and tasks

As Associate Project Manager, you will take responsibility for smaller projects from planning through delivery and close-out. You will coordinate customers, colleagues, suppliers and other stakeholders to keep projects moving according to scope, schedule, quality and financial targets.

The role gives you direct responsibility for the full project process while working closely with experienced colleagues across sales, engineering, procurement and operations. It is a good opportunity to develop your project management experience while gradually handling increasingly complex activities.

Your responsibilities will include

• Plan, coordinate and follow up on projects, ensuring activities and milestones progress according to the agreed scope and schedule.

• Act as a key contact for customers and coordinate across internal teams, suppliers and other project stakeholders.

• Monitor project financials, including costs, invoicing, cash flow and resource utilization.

• Identify and follow up on project risks, opportunities and changes, escalating when needed and taking corrective action together with the relevant stakeholders.

• Coordinate procurement of services, materials and equipment and support dialogue with suppliers throughout project execution.

• Maintain project schedules, track progress and promptly address potential delays that could affect on-time delivery.

• Ensure required project documentation, contractual obligations, quality requirements and HSE standards are followed.

• Support project acceptance and close-out and capture relevant lessons learned for future projects.

Qualifications for the role

• 
A relevant technical or commercial education combined with an interest in project management and project execution.

• 
Some experience with project management, project coordination or similar work. We also welcome candidates who are still building their project management experience.

• 
Ability to plan and coordinate activities and follow them through together with colleagues, customers and suppliers.

• 
An understanding of basic project economics, schedules and risk management, or an interest in developing these skills.

• 
Comfortable communicating with different stakeholders and keeping relevant people informed when priorities, deadlines or project conditions change.

• 
Comfortable working in English.

More information

At ABB, we have a clear goal of promoting diversity and inclusion in terms of gender, LGBTQ+, disability, ethnicity, and age. Together, we have embarked on a journey where we all individually and collectively celebrate and welcome individual differences. You can look forward to joining an organization that emphasizes employee well-being. Collaboration and team spirit are key words for us and a crucial foundation for reaching our shared goals. We prioritize a good working environment highly and continuously invest in the education and development of you and your colleagues. If you want to read more about our continuous work with the working environment and sustainability, you can find more information at: https://global.abb/group/en/sustainability

You will be based at our office in Middelfart, alongside your closest colleagues. In addition, we offer the possibility of working from home a few days a week.

Apply for the job online via our simple and easily accessible system, where you can also sign up to receive notifications on other opportunities within ABB. If you have questions about the position before then, you are welcome to contact Morten Hellesøe at +4540278387.

The application deadline is 10.12.2026. We look forward to receiving your application.

Do you want to build the operational backbone behind a new way of monetizing software - where pricing, product usage, data, and billing all need to connect seamlessly?

Trackunit is changing how we charge customers as we move from a traditional SaaS model towards more flexible, usage-based offerings. That means we need to connect a lot of moving parts: what customers use, how that usage is measured, what they have agreed to pay for, and what ultimately appears on their invoice.

As our Senior Monetization Operations Manager, you’ll help us make that entire flow work. You’ll build the processes and checks that help us catch errors early, keep our systems aligned, and give both customers and colleagues confidence that our billing is accurate.

This is a senior individual contributor role with a lot of ownership, but no formal people-management responsibility. You’ll work closely with colleagues across Product, Engineering, Data, Finance, Revenue & Billing and RevOps. Some of the foundations are still being built, so you won’t simply inherit a finished setup. You’ll have an important role in shaping how we work—and we hope that’s the kind of challenge you find energizing.

Trackunit is a fast-growing company and a leading supplier of IoT solutions, operating out of many offices worldwide. We create digital solutions that connect machines, people, and systems in the global construction industry, helping one of the world’s least digitalized industries become more connected, efficient, and productive.

With locations in Denmark, Germany and the Netherlands, we offer a flexible setup giving you the option to work from our hubs or remotely in these countries.

**What’s in it for you?

**

• A place in an agile growth SaaS business, with possibilities to grow internally in the company. We are moving quickly, so fasten your seat belt and prepare to adjust. Back in 2020 we were 150 employees at Trackunit and we have just passed 450 employees.

• International environment with regular check-ins and social events across teams, departments and borders.

• We take your personal and professional development goals seriously and support them through training, coaching and mindfulness, alongside an open feedback culture that helps you identify your strengths and opportunities. We do this by focusing on your impact on yourself, your team, and the organization.

• Flexibility and hybrid working is not just a cliché to us. We believe you know how you work best. Once you've decided what works for you, we'll make sure you have the IT equipment and support you need.

• Turning the Tide. At Trackunit, we aim to create and contribute to an inclusive workplace. This priority starts with our hiring - we do not discriminate on the basis of gender identity, sexual orientation, personal expression, ethnicity, religious belief, or disability status. We assess candidates solely on their qualifications and merit.

**Who are you ideally?

**We’re looking for a hands-on monetization operations expert who combines strong systems and data fluency with the ability to create structure across a complex, cross-functional environment.

**Ideally, You Bring

**

• Experience running or improving usage-based monetization operations, consumption platforms, metering, rating, or another environment where customer usage needs to be captured and processed accurately.

• The ability to follow data through several systems, spot when something doesn’t add up, and work out where the problem started - not just fix the final output.

• Experience setting up and testing products, price plans, usage rules, or similar configurations before they are released.

• A practical approach to processes and controls. You know how to make an operation reliable without creating unnecessary complexity or slowing everyone down.

• The confidence to bring Product, Engineering, Data, Finance, and commercial teams together when an issue crosses several areas - and to keep the work moving until the underlying cause has been resolved.

• Comfort working closely with both technical and commercial colleagues. You don’t need to be an engineer, but you should be curious about how data and systems work and willing to get into the details.

• The judgment to spot risks, challenge unclear ownership, and set clear standards, even when you don’t formally manage the people involved.

• Experience with usage-metering or monetization platforms such as m3ter, Metronome, Amberflo, or similar would be a strong advantage. Familiarity with Salesforce, NetSuite, Databricks, or related systems would also be valuable, but we don’t expect you to know our exact technology stack from day one.

Don't meet every single requirement? No worries - this is what we're looking for ideally, but if you're excited about this opportunity and your experience doesn't perfectly match every qualification, we'd still love to hear from you.

**Primary Responsibilities

****In this role, you will:

**

• Build and improve the way we run monetization operations, including clear processes, responsibilities, checks, and ways to escalate issues.

• Make sure new products and pricing plans are set up, tested, approved, and released correctly in m3ter and our connected systems.

• Keep track of whether the full flow from customer usage to invoice is working as expected and make risks or gaps visible early.

• Put the right checks in place to identify missing, incorrect, or unusual data before it affects customer billing.

• Work with Finance and Revenue & Billing to make sure the data and documentation needed for invoicing, reconciliation, and audits are ready and reliable.

• Help turn agreed business and pricing rules into system configurations and practical ways of working.

• Lead investigations when usage, system configuration, or billing numbers don’t look right, bringing the relevant teams together to find and fix the underlying cause.

• Work with Product, Engineering, and Data to improve how usage is captured, moved between systems, and monitored.

• Look for recurring problems and manual work that can be simplified or automated as the business grows.

**Our hiring process

• Virtual meet and greet with the hiring manager and someone from the team.

• Offer presentation and walk-through. We're excited to welcome you to Trackunit!

What you'll own

What you bring

**

• You've owned the direction of a technical area, including a significant rework.

**Nice To Have (none Of Them Required)

**

• Tools for scientists, or a background in bioinformatics, computational biology or AI for science

• Mastra or another TypeScript agent framework

• Open-weight models, through inference APIs or self-hosting

Our stack

TypeScript, Next.js and React. Python for our MCP service. An agent harness built on Mastra. Docker Compose and Kubernetes, hosted on Scaleway.

How we work

Our dev team is the two founders plus up to three new developers, led by our CTO. We discuss progress and priorities closely and continuously, and we expect you to take part: share ideas early, argue for what you think is right, and change course when the evidence says so.

Everything a lab builds in Dalea can be packaged and shared, so we're building a GitHub for life science: labs publish and reuse each other's workflows instead of rebuilding them from scratch. We work with biotech startups, academic labs, pharma R&D and CROs.

Timing and our funding round

This position depends on our current funding round closing, which we expect in February/March 2027. We can make a conditional offer before then, and we'll be open with you about the timing throughout the process.

• Warrants: under the Danish

Apply here with your LinkedIn profile, your CV and short answers to a few questions. No cover letter needed.

Tech-first. Ego-free. User-obsessed. Over a million Danes use Skatteguiden to understand and optimise their taxes: automating tax tracking, surfacing deductions people didn't know they had, and connecting directly to the Danish tax authority to do it. We're an independent, profitable, 50-person company in central Copenhagen with a 4.7-star rating and one mission: make financial insight accessible to everyone, not just those who can afford an accountant.

None of that works without data people can trust. Our platform runs on Snowflake, Dagster and dbt, and we're investing further in it. We're looking for a data engineer who wants to own it: build it, run it and keep improving it, from infrastructure and ingestion down to the SQL.

If you're ready for the step up to senior and want a platform that's yours to own, not one you build and hand over, this is it.

jobs.occupation: Assistant Professors in Electronic Systems (with the possibility of tenure-track)
jobs.description:
At the Technical Faculty of IT and Design, Department of Electronic Systems, one or more positions as Assistant Professor in Electronic Systems are open for appointments from June 1, 2027, or soon after. The positions are available for a period of 4 years (with the possibility of tenure-track). The positions are with the department's research groups located at the university campus in Copenhagen.

Your profile and work tasks

We seek to appoint one or more Assistant Professors (with the possibility of Tenure-Track) to conduct research, teaching, and knowledge exchange, and to grow and develop the department's research activities within our subject fields.

The positions require internationally recognized research experience within one or more of the following areas:

• Cyber security

• Privacy engineering

• Computer Systems

• Edge/cloud computing

• High-Performance Computing (HPC)

• Data Engineering

• Big Data Infrastructure

• Machine Learning Systems

The main tasks and responsibilities include:

• developing a research profile and providing valuable contributions to science.

• providing research-based teaching and supervision within at least one subject area.

• participating in grant application activities

• coordinating own projects and contributing to an active academic environment

Your competencies

You have an interest in collaborating with external partners and experience from participating in grant applications. You have also contributed to workplace well-being, collaboration, equal treatment, diversity, and a good working environment.

Selected candidates should demonstrate development potential in science and have peer-reviewed publications in recognized journals and books or anthologies. Under the leadership of others, you can plan and carry out individual teaching and supervision activities with a focus on the students' learning.

Who we are

In electronic engineering, Aalborg University is known worldwide for its high academic quality and societal impact. The Department of Electronic Systems employs more than 200 people, of which about 90 are PhD students, and about 40 % of all employees are internationals. In total, it has more than 700 students in its BSc and MSc programs, which are based on AAU's problem-based learning model.

The department leverages its unique research infrastructure and lab facilities to conduct world-leading fundamental and applied research within communication, networks, control systems, AI, sound, cyber security, and robotics. The department plays an active role in transferring inventions and results into applications in close collaboration with industrial partners worldwide.

The department places significant emphasis on supporting early career researchers and provides comprehensive career and personal development programmes, specifically designed to assist individual academics in achieving their professional objectives.

You can read more about the department at www.es.aau.dk.

Qualification requirements

Appointment as Assistant Professor requires academic qualifications at PhD level.

**Tenure-track

**When appointing tenure track assistant professors, Aalborg University also place particular emphasis on:

• The candidate can demonstrate a high degree of autonomy in their previous education and employment path

• The candidate shows considerable potential and is among the best in their field

• The candidate has academic experience from several universities and/or research institutions and preferably international experience

• The candidate is a skilled communicator

• The candidate writes and speaks English at the academic level

• The candidate is expected to meet the criteria for permanent employment as an associate professor at Aalborg University at the end of the tenure track process

Evaluation and promotion proces:

• Annual internal follow-ups to review progress on the promotion plan and ensure the assistant professor remains on track.

• A mid-term evaluation, based on external review, conducted by an internal assessment committee after three years.

• A final review by an external committee after 5.5 years. A positive outcome leads to a tenured appointment as Associate Professor.

• Assessment in connection with transfer to associate professorship

**Assessment in connection with transfer to associate professorship

**The assessment in connection with transition to tenure as an associate professor normally takes place in the final six months of the tenure track assistant professors’ employment. However, the employee may request that an assessment take place at an earlier time in the first four years. If this assessment finds that the employee is not academically qualified, they may request another assessment within the final six months of their period of employment. A maximum of two assessments may take place.

The assessment, on transition to the associate professorship, will as a minimum, emphasize the following qualifications in relation to the scientific subject area of the tenure track assistant professorship:

• Research qualifications equivalent to the level that can be achieved on the basis of satisfactorily completed employment as tenure track assistant professor.

• Documented scientific production at international level. Assessment will be based on up to ten selected publications selected by the employee.

• Documentation of pedagogical supervision and upgrading of qualifications, including a positive written assessment of teaching qualifications. The assessment will also be based on the employee's teaching portfolio.

• The level of contribution to an active academic environment as well as the ability to collaborate and build relationships.

• The level of experience with grant proposals and experience of communicating research to relevant stakeholders.

If the tenure track assistant professor fails to request that their qualifications be assessed in the last year of their period of employment or if they are assessed as not academically qualified, the university must immediately initiate dismissal proceedings in accordance with the collective agreement rules.

How to apply

Your application must include the following:

• Application, stating reasons for applying, qualifications in relation to the position, and intentions and visions for the position

• Curriculum Vitae (CV)

• Diplomas (master's degree diploma and PhD diploma)

• List of publications, with an indication of the attached publications that you wish to be taken into account in the assessment. You may attach a maximum of five publications.

• Documentation of teaching qualifications. Please see guidelines for teaching portfolio at The Technical Faculty of IT and Design. If this is not enclosed, the applicant must enclose the reasons for this .

• Dissemination qualifications, including participation on committees or boards, participation in organisations etc.

• Additional qualifications in relation to the position

• References/recommendations

You can read more about the requirements for your application here.

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position.

Aalborg University has a policy of parallel language use. The successful applicant is expected, with support from the university, to acquire Danish language skills over time and to be able to contribute to teaching in Danish within 2–5 years of employment, including grading and supervising students, at a level corresponding to the teaching undertaken.

Danish language courses will be offered as part of the employment.

Do you have any questions? If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.

 Further information

Read more about our recruitment process here

The appointment process at Aalborg University involves a shortlisting process. You can read more about the shortlisting and appointment process here.

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

Salary and terms of employment  The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement) and protocol on certain terms of employment of academic staff at universities.

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “Tenure track assistant professor/Tenure track researcher”.

jobs.description:
We invite applications for a full-time, one-year position as Research Assistant in the Section of Distributed, Embedded and Intelligent Systems (DEIS), Department of Computer Science, Aalborg University. The position focuses on developing reinforcement learning methods that produce understandable control strategies and provide insight into the underlying system dynamics and causal relationships. The research will address safe and effective control of cyber-physical systems, with particular emphasis on UPPAAL Stratego and collaboration with domain experts and external partners.

Expected starting date: 01.12.2026.

Your work tasks

You will develop and evaluate methods for explainable and causality informed reinforcement learning. The aim is to make learned strategies transparent to human domain experts, support well-founded trust in their decisions, and improve understanding of hidden dynamics and causal relationships in the systems being controlled. Your tasks will include:

• Developing compact, interpretable representations of learned control strategies, including strategy minimisation with guaranteed preservation of safety properties.

• Investigating how causal information can inform reinforcement learning and help explain the behaviour and decisions of learned strategies.

• Working with reinforcement learning and recurrent neural networks in UPPAAL Stratego, including implementation and experimental evaluation.

• Applying and evaluating the methods on safety-critical cyber-physical systems, with relevant case studies in water and wastewater infrastructure.

• Collaborating with DEIS researchers, the UPPAAL development team and external partners, and contributing to scientific publications and dissemination.

The work builds on DEIS research in safe reinforcement learning and practical experience with UPPAAL Stratego for modelling and optimal control of wastewater infrastructure, including collaboration with HOFOR continuing the DIREC Bridge project Verifiable and Safe AI.

Your competencies

You should have a strong background in reinforcement learning and machine learning, solid programming skills, and experience implementing and evaluating research methods. Knowledge of explainable AI, causal reasoning, recurrent neural networks, or interpretable policy representations is particularly relevant. Experience with UPPAAL or UPPAAL Stratego, formal verification, and modelling and control of cyber-physical systems is an advantage. You should be able to work independently, collaborate with researchers and domain experts, and communicate research clearly in English.

You will collaborate closely with development teams to ensure reliable software functionality in our hearing solutions. You will specify and verify embedded software tests, with a particular focus on test automation and the development of tools and test systems for firmware testing.

You will join Test Development, a team of 11 developers working closely with our Agile teams. Together, we develop, specify and verify features and integrated product platforms to ensure robust software functionality in new devices and products.

**

• Specify, plan, execute and evaluate embedded software tests, and communicate findings clearly to development teams

• Verify the behaviour of signal processing algorithms, wireless protocols and operating systems

• Review software requirements and design documentation to support testable, reliable solutions

• Follow up on test results and provide clear reporting and input to developers

• Contribute to compliance with internal requirements, relevant standards and regulations

• Develop and improve test automation, tools and test environments for firmware testing

• Collaborate with Agile teams to improve testing processes and support effective software delivery

**

• Have experience with software testing, verification and test automation using C#, or another object-oriented programming language

• Bring a structured and proactive approach to planning work, following through on activities and improving ways of working

We pride ourselves on encouraging flexible work whenever possible. We trust our people to fulfill their responsibilities, to know when in-person collaboration is better than hybrid, and to be present when it's needed most.
